# Gabe Vandevere

> Gabe Vandevere is a senior computer science student at the University of Delaware (expected spring 2027, GPA 3.87, Dean's List every semester) based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, in the Philadelphia area. He is a QA and Operations Intern at The RxAssistant, where he builds and tests AI-powered solutions for pharmaceutical clients, and previously a Research and Development Intern at Westpepper Capital, where he built machine-learning backtesting pipelines and real-time crypto market-data systems. His own projects run from clinical computer vision to systems programming in C. His website is served from a Jetson Orin Nano on his desk, which also runs the language model visitors can talk to.

## Experience

- **QA and Operations Intern, The RxAssistant** (remote; 2026-05 to present): Develops and deploys AI-powered solutions for pharmaceutical clients across more than ten brands: client-facing conversational-AI prototypes and production demos, ambient listening and workflow automation, conversational AI over regulated product, access, affordability and patient-support content. Assists QA and UAT for client releases (authored and executed 100+ test cases, validated AI responses, supported deployments from staging through production). Contributes to product infrastructure including React Native setup and AWS Bedrock integration.
- **Research and Development Intern, Westpepper Capital** (Radnor, Pennsylvania; 2025-06 to 2026-02): Built an end-to-end machine-learning modeling and backtesting pipeline over earnings, guidance and analyst-estimate data (15 model variants, up to 57% next-day direction accuracy in historical tests). Designed and deployed real-time crypto order-book tracking in Java on AWS EC2 via the Kraken API across 200+ markets. Developed trading strategies, one promoted to production. Built a Python analytics pipeline and dashboard (P&L and volume aggregation, Matplotlib) used daily.

## Projects

- **Savor**: An AI pantry application built over one weekend at HenHacks 2026 with three teammates. It reads a grocery receipt with Google Gemini's vision model, keeps the inventory in Supabase, suggests meals around whatever is closest to expiring, and totals the money and carbon saved. Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, Tailwind, deployed on DigitalOcean. Source: https://devpost.com/software/savor-jby10r
- **Dog gait analysis and CCL detection**: Takes a video of a dog walking and says whether its cranial cruciate ligament is torn — the most common orthopaedic injury in dogs, normally diagnosed by eye. Two parts, both his: a two-stage pose cascade that tracks 39 body keypoints and 46 facial landmarks frame by frame, landing mean landmark error 28.6% below the single-model version it replaced (PCK@5% 71.0% to 84.1% on 479 held-out images); and a classifier trained on 12 GB of clinical video that turns those joint trajectories into gait features and calls CCL against normal. It rejects footage not shot side-on and writes a pose-overlaid copy of the video so a clinician can check what the model was looking at. Source: https://github.com/gabe-udel/dog-emotions
- **Oracle**: A Paper Minecraft server running on a Raspberry Pi 4B at home, reachable by friends over the public internet through an outbound tunnel rather than router port forwarding, and managed as a systemd unit that sends stop first so the world saves before a restart. On top of it, a Java plugin with no command and no prefix: it reads every public chat line, scores it 0-100 on whether it is worth answering, and speaks only when a line clears the threshold and it is off cooldown. It notices deaths, advancements and slower behavioural patterns, and swaps between Claude, Gemini and a local Jetson model without a restart.

### What has Gabe Vandevere built?

Three that he leads with: Savor, an AI pantry app built at HenHacks 2026 that reads grocery receipts with Google Gemini's vision model and suggests meals around whatever is closest to expiring; a pipeline that takes a video of a dog walking and says whether its cranial cruciate ligament is torn, which he built end to end — the pose cascade that tracks 39 body keypoints and 46 facial landmarks, and the classifier trained on 12 GB of clinical video that reads gait from it; and Oracle, a Paper Minecraft server he runs on a Raspberry Pi 4B with a Java plugin on it that scores every line of chat and decides for itself when it is worth speaking.
